open_points.subject: A18
open_points.text: The process looks at the clock at least once a minute;
open_points.question: What clock measures that minute, and on what exact cadence or triggering rule must the process read it?
options: Poll every 60 seconds of a suspend-aware monotonic clock.
Poll on UTC wall-clock minute boundaries.
Poll more frequently on an implementation-chosen cadence, provided no interval exceeds one minute.
open_points.default_guess: Poll on each UTC minute boundary, using a suspend-aware monotonic wait between polls and an immediate wall-clock read after every wake.

witness.initial: Registry is running before 03:00 UTC and no kept backup exists for the date.
events: One implementation polls on the next UTC minute boundary; another polls every ten seconds from an implementation-chosen phase.
outcomes: The run starts during the first ten seconds after 03:00 UTC, producing a different snapshot and recorded instant.
witness.observer: The owner, through the newest-backup instant and the records included in the backup.

open_points.subject: A18
open_points.text: The cutoff and each record's UTC instant (L16) are compared as instants at the full precision each holds, neither rounded nor truncated;
open_points.question: What exact representation and precision must the backup record and the cutoff use, so that choosing the precision is not left to the implementer?
options: The native precision of the injected wall-clock source, encoded losslessly in the record.
open_points.default_guess: Use UTC datetimes with fixed microsecond precision and encode that precision losslessly in every readable backup record.

witness.initial: A snapshot occurs at an instant 719 hours, 59 minutes, 59.6 seconds before a later retention cutoff.
events: One implementation records snapshot instants to whole seconds; another records microseconds.
The retention step reads its cutoff and compares each stored instant without changing the precision that implementation chose.
outcomes: The whole-second record falls before the cutoff and the backup is deleted.
The microsecond record remains after the cutoff and the backup is kept.
witness.observer: The owner, who sees whether the kept backup remains.

open_points.subject: A18
open_points.text:
With the step's cutoff fixed at its start, a kept backup made exactly
   30 × 24 hours before it is kept and one made a second earlier is deleted.
open_points.question: What Required tests item must demonstrate that retention compares subsecond or otherwise finer stored precision without rounding or truncation?
options: Add cases immediately on both sides of the cutoff at the mandated smallest time unit.
Add a case where the cutoff and record carry different permitted precisions and state the required result.
Mandate one precision first, then test values one unit on either side of the cutoff.
open_points.default_guess: Mandate microsecond precision and test backups one microsecond before, exactly at, and one microsecond after the cutoff.

witness.initial: The cutoff and backup instants differ by less than one second.
events: An implementation rounds or truncates both values to seconds before comparing them.
The listed test is run only with an exact-cutoff backup and a backup one full second earlier.
outcomes: The implementation passes the listed test despite violating the rule against rounding or truncation.
A full-precision implementation also passes the same test.
witness.observer: The test suite cannot distinguish the two implementations.
